prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1217; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact at an intersection, with the insured vehicle struck on the driver's side by a vehicle that failed to yield. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact and lists the same sequence of events the claimant described at intake.

Entry 4: Scene photographs were obtained and confirm several details of the collision. No independent witnesses have been identified beyond the parties and responding officers.

Entry 5: Vehicle damage on the driver's side is consistent with the reported impact angle and location. No prior damage to the same panels is recorded in the claim history or in the photos on file.

Entry 6: Claimant reports a shoulder injury. The kind of injury and the force involved in the crash appear to align well, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known from the medical history provided.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits tapering off as the claimant's condition improved. The claimant's account has remained the same in every conversation to date.

Entry 8: Medical records and billing have been requested through counsel. Reserves are being reviewed against the treatment timeline as records arrive.

Entry 9: File remains open pending receipt of the complete medical records and the attorney's demand package. Next review is scheduled once those documents are received.
